brief: Two headlines in roughly 36 hours, Talen naming Terry Nutt CEO with a $1.5 billion buyback, and Constellation (CEG) and Amazon announcing a 20-year power purchase deal, follow a quiet stretch for power headlines, which GS thinks should draw attention into earnings preview season. Power IPP stocks have been challenging year-to-date despite no real change to medium- to longer-term fundamentals and power curves moving higher. GS says specialists are generally neutral on the group while generalists lean more cautious, though sentiment can turn quickly. The CEG-Amazon deal adds only a low-single-digit percentage to 2027 free cash flow on GS numbers but is read as a step in the right direction, giving the group a heartbeat (CEG +4% pre-market). PJM September peak power cleared at $128, 47% above its level entering the month, and Cal27-Cal29 strips also moved higher, reinforcing forward power demand. GS still sees the power infrastructure setup as robust and views the BTM-versus-IPP rotation as not mutually exclusive. Separately, a coalition including Blackstone QTS, NextEra, Siemens Energy, Quanta, NEI and Lancium is pushing back on Texas data-center opposition, noting $200bn of US projects were blocked in H1 and about 90% of new ERCOT power connection requests come from data centers.
